scenarios.setup: Same subagent rung as S6, but the lane carries neither a scored `tier:` nor an authoring `default_tier:` in team.yaml. You still stamp the producer marker. What do you put in GUILD_TIER on the dispatch env?
scenarios.note: issue #91: omit rather than fabricate — the tier guard verifies the dispatched model AGAINST a declared GUILD_TIER, so a made-up tier makes the guard check the model against a fiction. Absent tier records `model_present`, which is correct.

scenarios.setup: Same subagent rung as S6, but the lane's owner is `kb-viz-engineer`, whose TEAM-file entry carries `definition_source: project` and `definition: .guild/agents/kb-viz-engineer.md`. How do you construct the Agent() call — subagent_type, prompt line 1, and the rest of the prompt?
scenarios.note: issue #91 codex round-1 finding 2: a project specialist dispatches as the host-generic type with (a) line 1 = `GUILD_AGENT_DEFINITION=<the team-file definition path>` AND (b) the human-readable adoption instruction buildPrompt emits (read it FIRST and adopt it fully + load project-local skills). The marker alone satisfies the #58 guard but leaves the agent generic — syntactically compliant, functionally persona-stripped. Both, always.

scenarios.setup: Same subagent rung. You need `definition_source` and `definition` to choose the subagent_type and the line-1 marker. The plan lane gives you `owner: kb-viz-engineer`, `task-id`, `depends-on`, `scope`. Name BOTH: where those two values come from, AND what you do when the lookup fails or the project specialist's `definition` is not the role-matched `.guild/agents/kb-viz-engineer.md` path. Answer with the source AND the failure behavior together.
scenarios.note: issue #91 codex rounds 1-3, finding 1: `definition_source`/`definition` are TEAM-file fields on `specialists[]`, keyed by `name` — NOT lane fields. Join `team.specialists.find(s => s.name === lane.owner)` AND FAIL CLOSED — abort the lane — on no match, or when the project specialist's definition is not the role-matched `.guild/agents/<name>.md` (absent / arbitrary / role-mismatched). Normalize the path ONCE (trim) and use that normalized value for BOTH carriers: `composeInProcessDispatch` compares trimmed, so a padded-but-canonical path passes validation, and emitting the RAW field would then produce a malformed line-1 marker the whole-line parser rejects. Grading requires BOTH halves: naming the source but continuing after a failed lookup is a FAIL, because that is what dispatches a project specialist under an unregistered name.

scenarios.setup: Three re-dispatch situations in one run on the subagent rung: (a) a lane failed its receipt check and `## Lane retry + dead-lettering` says retry; (b) a dead-lettered lane is resumed later; (c) a silent lane is replaced by a nudge-replacement spawn. What does EACH of the three Agent() calls carry?
scenarios.note: issue #91: all three are NEW Agent() calls and each needs BOTH marker halves (env + prompt line 1), plus the project-class adoption instruction where applicable. Answering for the retry alone is incomplete — an unmarked resume or nudge-replacement re-opens exactly the gap the marker closes.
